newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY ON BROADWAY FOR NEW SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY ON BROADWAY FOR NEW SEASON.

text.p: The Great One is starring in a Broadway revival this season, a superstar reunion that should spice up the 79th National Hockey League campaign opening on Friday.

Wayne Gretzky, arguably hockey's greatest player ever, takes his slick moves and perfect passes to New York this year to hook up again with former Edmonton Oilers partner and resident Rangers superstar captain Mark Messier.
There is an air of electricity in New York as the Great One, holder of 62 NHL records including most career goals, assists and points, brings his act to the Big Apple.
Critics say the 35-year-old Gretzky's skills have greatly diminished. However, he only really suffers in comparisons with himself.
Playing for mediocre teams in Los Angeles and St Louis last season, Gretzky still cracked the 100-point mark.

He longs for one more Stanley Cup, and playing alongside Messier, with whom Gretzky won four championships in Edmonton, gives him a realistic shot at number five. Messier is going for his seventh Stanley Cup ring.
Meanwhile, the Stanley Cup resides in Denver, the Winnipeg Jets are in Phoenix and flying rats will be frowned upon as the 1996-97 NHL season kicks off.

Following the thrilling U.S. victory in the World Cup that severely bruised Canada's national psyche, the NHL will settle in for the long, gruelling regular season with a feeling that the balance of power has shifted below the 49th parallel.
Further fanning the flames of Canadian fears that the NHL is abandoning its spiritual homeland, the Winnipeg Jets begin their new life in the U.S. sun belt as the Phoenix Coyotes.
That adds insult to the injury inflicted by the Stanley Cup victory of the Colorado Avalanche, who had spent most of the previous two decades in the French-Canadian hockey bastion of Quebec.
The Rangers should be pushed in the tough Atlantic Division all season by Eric Lindros and his physical Philadelphia Flyers and the talented, young Florida Panthers.
The Panthers, led by the stellar goaltending of John Vanbiesbrouck, stunned the NHL by reaching the Stanley Cup finals in only their third year of existance.
Exuberant Panthers fans showering thousands of toy rats onto the ice after every goal inspired the latest NHL rules change.

Long delays caused by throwing of objects onto the ice can now result in a delay of game penalty against the home team. It remains to be seen whether the penalty threat will curtail Miami's rain of rodents or the octopus tossing in Detroit.
The Pittsburgh Pengins were heartened by the decision of superstar centre Mario Lemieux to return for another season.

Lemieux and brilliant Czech winger Jaromir Jagr battled last season for the goal scoring title. Lemieux finished first with Jagr second. And for much of the year, Pittsburgh teammate Ron Francis was third in overall scoring.
The defence may be suspect, but with Lemieux and Jagr running the powerplay, the Penguins are a serious Stanley Cup contender and the team to beat in Northeast Division.
Detroit has been favoured to win the last three seasons, and posted the best record in the league the last two, including a record 62 victories in the 1995-96 campaign.

But the Central Division powerhouse Red Wings keep coming up short. Deep in Russian talent, critics question the heart and desire of Russian stars who turned in a disappointing effort in the otherwise hotly contested World Cup.

The Avalanche are the team to beat in the West with an extremely talented nucleus led by Patrick Roy, one of game's great goaltenders, emerging superstar Joe Sakic, crafty veteran Claude Lemieux and a host of worthy role players.
Vancouver could rejoin the contenders club with the return of Russian Rocket Pavel Bure, who led the league with 60 goals two years ago.

There is great anticipation of the union of Bure and fellow-Russian sniper, Alexander Mogilny, a coupling that was short-circuited last year when Bure was lost for the entire season with a knee injury.
